I've been farming this land for 45 years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil. I know when to plant by the feel of the air and the color of the sky. No one needs to tell me what to do — I've done this more times than I can count.

My farm is small, 3.5 mu. My son works in the city now. It's just me and my wife. I can't manage too much complexity. I do what works and has always worked here in Quzhou.

**Wheat (winter crop):** I plant every October after the maize comes off. I'll buy the improved wheat seed from the village supply cooperative — the local recommended variety. I've tried saving my own seed but the yields started dropping, so I buy new seed every few years. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer when I prepare the bed, then push urea at jointing time in the spring. I've done this for decades. I'll irrigate before winter sets in to protect the roots from freezing, again at jointing, and again when heads are filling out. Three times is what I always do. I'll spray for aphids once in May if I see them — I usually do. I use rotary tillage to turn the stubble in. I expect around 450 jin per mu — that's normal for my land.

**Maize (summer crop):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant maize. I always use hybrid seed — everyone around here does now, yields are much better than the old varieties. Same fertilizer approach: base fertilizer at planting, urea side-dressed when the plant is knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat if summer rains are decent, but I'll pump the well once or twice depending on how dry it gets. I'll spray for armyworm if needed — once is usually enough. I don't do deep tillage for maize, just rotary after wheat harvest to break up the surface. I expect 550-600 jin per mu.

The plan doesn't change much year to year. Small farm, two old people, keep it simple and reliable.
